issues.detail: Hebrew 'נָדִיב' means 'generous/noble person', not '君王' (king). The Chinese renders it as 'king', which changes the referent from a generous person to a monarch.

Hebrew 'וְכָל הָרֵעַ' means 'and every friend/companion' (from רֵעַ, friend), not '一切弟兄' (all brothers). The Chinese substitutes 'brothers' for 'friends/companions', altering the relationship described.

Hebrew 'לְאִישׁ מַתָּן' means 'to a man of gifts' (i.e., a briber or gift-giver), not '那送禮物的人' (the one who gives gifts). The Chinese rendering is close but the phrase 'אִישׁ מַתָּן' specifically refers to a person who gives gifts/bribes, and the Chinese '那送禮物的人' is acceptable, but the main issue is the first two changes.
